## Context

The `COMMITS` event and `attach_commits` reducer already exist (`rebar.attach_commits`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:697`, re-exported from `src/rebar/__init__.py`), used by the code-review workflow. Missing: an author-facing repair surface for a botched `rebar-ticket:` trailer, plus a consumer. Approved design (b902-18af-14ed-4da1): expose retroactive commit linking on CLI + library + MCP, document it, then add a deterministic close-gate check that linked commits' diffs match the recorded `file_impact`. OUT of scope: linked commits as a completion-verifier diff basis (they may be incomplete; CV already prefetches from `file_impact`).

## Plan

1. **Shared DET module** `src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py` (new, ~120 LOC): (a) `invalid_commit_shas(shas, repo_root)` via `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}`; (b) the step-4 path matchers, including `glob_match` — the `**/`-aware semantics (`fnmatch(p,g) or (g.startswith("**/") and fnmatch(p,g[3:]))`) from `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py:746`. Its ONLY true mirror is `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:242`; `src/rebar/grounding/oracle.py:316` uses PLAIN `fnmatch`, is NOT a copy, and is left untouched. The DET path must not import `rebar.llm` (optional `[agents]` extra), so the helper is hoisted here and BOTH real copies (`prompts._glob_match`, `registry._glob_match`) become thin delegating wrappers — one implementation.

2. **CLI verb** `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>...` wrapping the seam. Add to `_WRITES_FULL` in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`; add a variadic handler (N SHAs) to `_ARGV_REGISTRY` in `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py`; ship pinned help `src/rebar/_cli/help/attach-commits.txt` + the `overview.txt` line (golden-pinned; `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py` requires it). Thin body in `src/rebar/_commands/attach_commits.py`.

3. **Validation in the SEAM, not the CLI**, so all three surfaces inherit it: `rebar.attach_commits` calls `commit_impact.invalid_commit_shas` before appending. **ALL-OR-NOTHING** — the batch is validated first; if any SHA fails, NO `COMMITS` event is recorded and the call raises naming every offender. Union-add unchanged. Library: `rebar.attach_commits` is already re-exported — confirm and document. MCP: register `attach_commits` in `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` with an `AttachCommitsResultOut` outputSchema in `src/rebar/_mcp_models.py`, per the existing write-tool pattern (`mcp_server.py` only assembles registrars).

4. **DET close check** in the existing completion precheck `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` — the module that today raises "cannot confirm the work landed" (there is no `src/rebar/workflow/close_gate.py`). Discovery unions the two existing sources: (i) `state.commits` from COMMITS events; (ii) the precheck's referencing-commit scan (`_referencing_commit_exists`, `close_precheck.py:186` — commits reachable from HEAD carrying a `rebar-ticket:` trailer or leading `<id>:` subject for the ticket or any transitive descendant). It returns only a bool, so it is refactored into a SHA-returning `_referencing_commits(...)` with `_referencing_commit_exists` kept as a thin wrapper — the documented monkeypatch target and its call sites keep working unchanged. For each commit, `git show --name-only` gives changed paths; a path neither covered by `file_impact` nor matched by this check's OWN exemption globs (`tests/**`, `docs/**`, `**/*.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — owned here, not inherited) is a deterministic BLOCK naming the commit and paths. Matching (via step 1, not re-derived): normalized repo-relative POSIX paths; a `file_impact` entry matches on exact equality, or as a directory prefix when it ends with `/` or names an existing directory; exemptions use `**/`-aware `glob_match`. No substring matching. No LLM.

   **Git errors, asymmetric by source:** a source-(ii) commit is local by construction, so a `git show` failure FAILS CLOSED (block, naming the SHA). A source-(i) SHA may legitimately be absent locally (another clone, or unfetched), so it is SKIPPED — blocking a foreign SHA would false-positive on a surface built to record commits.

   **Scope symmetry.** Source-(ii) discovery credits commits for the ticket OR any transitive descendant (`accepted_ids`, `close_precheck.py:361-367`), but `field_reads.file_impact(ticket_id, tracker)` (`field_reads.py:36`) reads only THIS ticket's — reusing it as-is would false-BLOCK a parent declaring `file_impact` when children's commits touch child-owned paths. So the check compares against the UNION of `file_impact` over the SAME id set discovery uses, making both scopes match by construction.

   A ticket with no discovered commits keeps today's behavior. The check is skipped when the union is empty.

5. **Remedy for a legitimate block:** the message names the offending paths and says to declare them via `rebar set-file-impact <ticket> …`, after which close proceeds; `--force="<reason>"` stays the break-glass.

6. **Docs.** `docs/cli-reference.md` is GENERATED (`scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`, CI drift gate, subcommand count in header) so it is regenerated, not hand-edited. Hand-edited: `docs/mcp-reference.md` and `src/rebar/_guides/commit-ticket-trailer.md`. Each names the verb, its use, and the step-5 remedy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>` records a COMMITS event that `rebar show` reflects. Verify: `pytest tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py -x`.
- [ ] An invalid SHA is rejected with an error naming it. Verify: same file, test asserting the offending SHA appears in the error text.
- [ ] A batch containing any invalid SHA records nothing (all-or-nothing). Verify: test asserting `state.commits` is byte-identical before/after a mixed valid/invalid batch.
- [ ] The MCP server exposes `attach_commits` with an outputSchema, routed through the same seam. Verify: the MCP tool-inventory test asserts `"attach_commits"` is in the registered tool names.
- [ ] A commit touching a path outside the declared `file_impact` blocks close, naming it. Verify: unit test asserting the exact path string in the raised message.
- [ ] A commit whose paths are all declared does not block. Verify: unit test asserting close proceeds.
- [ ] An exempt path does not block, incl. at repo root (`README.md` under `**/*.md`). Verify: unit test per exemption glob.
- [ ] The DET check imports no `rebar.llm` module. Verify: test asserting `[m for m in sys.modules if m.startswith("rebar.llm")] == []` in a fresh interpreter.
- [ ] The `**/`-aware glob semantics have one implementation. Verify: test asserting `prompts._glob_match` and `registry._glob_match` both delegate to `commit_impact.glob_match`.
- [ ] An unreadable source-(ii) commit fails closed naming the SHA; an unresolvable source-(i) SHA is skipped without blocking. Verify: one unit test per direction.
- [ ] `docs/mcp-reference.md` names the `attach_commits` tool. Verify: `pytest tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py -k docs_mcp` (asserts the literal `attach_commits` occurs in the file).
- [ ] The commit-trailer guide names the verb. Verify: `pytest tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py -k docs_guide_verb` (asserts the literal `rebar attach-commits` occurs).
- [ ] The commit-trailer guide names the `set-file-impact` remedy. Verify: `pytest tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py -k docs_guide_remedy` (asserts the literal `rebar set-file-impact` occurs).
- [ ] A parent close does not block on a path declared only in a child's `file_impact`. Verify: unit test closing a parent whose child commit touches a child-declared path, asserting no block.
- [ ] `_referencing_commit_exists` keeps its bool contract after the refactor. Verify: unit test asserting it returns True/False identically for a matching and a non-matching id set while `_referencing_commits` returns the SHAs.
- [ ] `docs/cli-reference.md` is regenerated and its drift gate passes. Verify: `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check` exits 0.
